deep.reconstruction:
Setting. pi is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}. Its generators l_0, l_1, l_infinity are inertia loops satisfying l_0 l_1 l_infinity = 1, so pi is free profinite on l_0 and l_1. S_3 acts on pi by outer automorphisms. Let rho be the order-3 rotation l_0 -> l_1 -> l_infinity -> l_0. Rho is a genuine automorphism, since l_1 l_infinity l_0 = 1 is a conjugate of the defining relation. Grothendieck wants to parametrize the outer automorphisms of pi that preserve inertia and commute with the canonical S_3 action. This is the program that later became the Grothendieck-Teichmüller group.

Normalization. On the previous page every outer automorphism is represented by an automorphism u normalizing L_0 = <l_0>, unique up to int(lambda) with lambda in L_0. Its multiplier is p = chi(u) in Zhat*, so (*) u(l_0) = l_0^p. Commutation with rho up to inner automorphisms is written (**) u rho = int(g) rho u, which fixes g uniquely.

This page:
1. Ambiguity of g. Replacing u by int(lambda) u, with lambda = l_0^alpha, replaces g by lambda g rho(lambda)^{-1} = l_0^alpha g l_1^{-alpha}.
2. u in terms of (p, g). The relations (*) and (**) give:
   - u(l_1) = u rho(l_0) = int(g) l_1^p;
   - u(l_infinity) = u rho(l_1) = int(g) int(rho(g)) l_infinity^p = int(g rho(g)) l_infinity^p.
3. Condition for an endomorphism. The images must satisfy the defining relation:
   - l_0^p · int(g) l_1^p · int(g rho g) l_infinity^p = 1;
   - equivalently l_0^p g l_1^p rho(g) l_infinity^p rho(g)^{-1} g^{-1} = 1;
   - equivalently, after conjugating, int(g^{-1}) l_0^p · l_1^p · int(rho(g)) l_infinity^p = 1.
4. Consistency. (*) and (**) then hold by construction. For (**) it suffices to check the arguments l_0 and l_1, since they generate pi.

Continuation (next page). Grothendieck notes that proving such a pair (p; g) gives an automorphism rather than just an endomorphism 'seems delicate'. He then adds commutation with the transposition sigma_infinity (l_0 <-> l_1). This yields h = g l_1^q and the condition that some q exists with g l_1^q sigma_infinity(g) in L_0.

In modern terms this is a (lambda, f)-type parametrization of the group of S_3-equivariant, inertia-preserving outer automorphisms of Fhat_2. The 3-cycle relation here is the analogue of Drinfeld's hexagon relation (II); the 2-cycle condition is the analogue of relation (I). The candidate group is essentially GThat_0 (Drinfeld's relations without the pentagon), worked out in spring 1981.
errors: No mathematical error in the computations; each step checks out (the change of g under int(lambda), the formulas for u(l_1) and u(l_infinity), and the expanded relation).
The image writes alpha in Zhat^*; it should be alpha in Zhat, since lambda is an arbitrary element of L_0 = Zhat.

Notation slip relative to the previous page: there (**) is written with tau, while on this page the computation uses rho (the order-3 rotation). The next page confirms the intended relation involves rho, and the tau case is treated as an example (tau rho = int(l_1) rho tau).
Gap, acknowledged on the next page: bijectivity of the endomorphism defined by (p, g) is not established.

ideas.what: Parametrize inertia-preserving outer automorphisms of profinite pi_{0,3} commuting with the order-3 rotation by pairs (p, g) in Zhat* x pi. Here p is the cyclotomic multiplier and g is the conjugating element, with the normalization ambiguity g -> l_0^a g l_1^{-a}.
ideas.modern_name: (lambda, f) parametrization of GThat (Drinfeld) / Ihara's description of the Galois image in Out(Fhat_2)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1990-91); the Galois-action form goes back to Belyi and Ihara (1980s)
ideas.where_published: The idea of studying Gal(Qbar/Q) via automorphisms of pi_{0,3} commuting with S_3 appears in La Longue Marche (1981) and Esquisse d'un programme (1984). The explicit (p, g) relation on this page is not, to my knowledge, in circulated texts.

ideas.what: Cyclic (3-cycle) relation l_0^p g l_1^p rho(g) l_infinity^p rho(g)^{-1} g^{-1} = 1 as the condition for (p, g) to define an endomorphism.
ideas.modern_name: Hexagon relation (II) of GThat: f(z,x) z^m f(y,z) y^m f(x,y) x^m = 1

ideas.what: Endomorphism vs automorphism issue (next page: 'ça semble délicat').
ideas.modern_name: GThat defined as the invertible elements of the monoid of solutions

ideas.what: Extra condition from the transposition: there exists q with g l_1^q sigma_infinity(g) in L_0.
ideas.modern_name: Relation (I) of GThat (f(x,y) f(y,x) = 1) after normalization; the group defined by (I) and (II) is GThat_0

missed.claim: In spring 1981 Grothendieck explicitly derived the (multiplier, conjugating element) parametrization of S_3-commuting outer automorphisms of pi_{0,3}. He also obtained the 3-cycle relation equivalent to Drinfeld's hexagon relation, nine years before Drinfeld's GThat.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This documents that the defining relations (I) and (II) of GThat_0, not just the philosophy, were written by Grothendieck in 1981. That bears on the attribution and history of the Grothendieck-Teichmüller group.

missed.claim: Grothendieck identified, but did not resolve, the problem of showing that a solution (p, g) gives an automorphism. Drinfeld later sidestepped this by taking invertible elements of the monoid.
missed.quote: Mais comment vérifier que (ρ;g) définissent non seulement un endomorphisme, mais un automorphisme ? Ça semble délicat...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Whether every solution of relations (I) and (II) in the profinite setting is automatically invertible is a natural question, and to my knowledge it is not standardly addressed (the monoid definition is used instead).

deep.surprise_reason: Grothendieck's interest in the S_3-equivariant automorphisms of pi_{0,3} is known from La Longue Marche and the Esquisse. Seeing the explicit (p, g) parametrization and the hexagon-type relation worked out in 1981 is a notable unpublished detail anticipating Drinfeld. Specialists like Schneps may already be aware of similar computations in the Longue Marche, so I stay moderate.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'si on remplace g par int(λ)u' should read 'si on remplace u par int(λ)u'.
'α ∈ Ẑ^*': the image looks like Ẑ^* but mathematically it should be α ∈ Ẑ.
In the boxed line and later, 'int(g ρ(g))' is correct; the right-margin note reads 'int(gρ(g)) l_∞^p' as the final value of u(l_∞).

The final paragraph reads 'Les relations (*) et (**) sont vérifiées par construction (pour **, il suffit en effet de les vérifier pour les valeurs aux deux arguments l_0, l_1)'. A crossed-out symbol precedes the (**), which is retained.
The marginal NB is largely illegible; it plausibly says one does not have to verify explicitly that the maps respect the multiplicators p.
